div.head: II As 15
div.ab: Feorðe: þæt nan scyldwyrhta ne lecge nan scepes fel on scyld; ⁊ gif he hit dó, gilde XXX scll'.
Be scyldwyrhtum. We cwædon, þæt nán scyldwyrhta ne lecge nán sceapes felle on scyld; ⁊ gif he hit dó, gylde XXX scill.
[Be scyld . . .] Feorðe: þæt nan . . . ecgge nan scepes fell on sceld; ⁊ gif he hit . . .
De scuta facientibus. Et nullus scyldƿyrhta (id est scutum faciens) ponat pellem ouis in scuto. Si quis hoc faciat, emendet XXX sol.
[Be scyldwyrhtum.] Feorðe: þæt nan scyldwyrhta ne lecge nan scepes fel on scyld; ⁊ gif he hit dó, gilde XXX scll'.
(Von Schildmachern. So Ld) Viertens (Wir bestimmten Ld): dass kein Schildmacher ein Schafsfell auf den Schild lege; und wenn er es thut, zahle er 30 Schill. [dem König].
(Of shield-makers. So Ld) Fourthly (We determined, Ld): that no shield-maker put a sheepskin on a shield; and if he does it, let him pay 30 shillings [to the king].
Fourthly: [we declare] that no shield-maker shall cover a shield with sheepskin. If he does he shall pay 30 shillings.
Fourthly: that no shieldmaker is to put any sheepskin on a shield, and if he does so, he is to pay 30 shillings.

S. Gl Fell 2; Schild 4. Die Rüstung des Volks soll dauerhaft sein. Auf diesen Satz bezieht sich III 8. Auch II 13. 16. 18 sorgen für die Wehrkraft. Über den Agsā. Schild in Funden s. Fairholt Costume in Engl. 49; Baye Industrie Anglosax. 37

See Gl Fell 2; Schild 4. The people’s armour is to be durable. III 8 refers to this sentence. II 13. 16. 18 also provide for military strength. On the Anglo-Saxon shield in finds see Fairholt Costume in Engl. 49; Baye Industrie Anglosax. 37
